question: Build a bridge probe per entity and measure how much of it the J-lens dictionary explains.

lens.vector: v_t = (g * W_U[t]) @ J++_l, unit-normalised; g = final-norm gain (1 + weight)

prompt_format: raw text, no chat template, no special tokens added
filter: keep a prompt if the first word of Qwen's greedy continuation (8 tokens) equals an accepted answer, case-insensitively
probe: mean final-token residual (block output) over kept prompts minus the mean over entities

decomposition.method: non-negative OMP, NNLS refit each step
decomposition.dictionary: unit J++ vectors of non-special tokens whose decode has a letter

metrics: fraction of probe variance in the J-part per layer
chance level of that fraction: the same decomposition of isotropic random directions (one per probed entity per layer, seed 0)
whether the entity's own token is among its J-part atoms
deviations: J-lens vectors include the final-norm gain g (the reference omits it); g rescales dimensions unevenly, so these are the directions the lens's readout actually uses.
Added (not in the plan): the random-direction chance level for the J-part share.
Entity prompts were written by the coding agent and pass the mechanical checks in data.py; the human has not reviewed them yet.
Top-up round: prompts were added for the entities above after seeing run v1's filter results for them (the plan allows one logged round).

Second prompt round beyond the plan's one top-up: ~20 more prompts per entity, written after two failed exp02 gates (mean-difference probes 17%, whitened 8%; exp02_swaps/gate_debug*: ~6-prompt means are mostly prompt noise). Chosen by the human. Written by coding subagents, checked mechanically, not human-reviewed.

New check (a stricter reading of 'never names the entity'): no prompt word or accepted answer may be built on the entity's name (first five letters, or irregular forms such as Chinese/French/nitrate; data.py). The earlier prompts that break it are dropped (listed above; they were in runs v1-v2), as are 18 new prompts that broke it before pinning.
J++ decomposition: run v3's probes are rebuilt (its cache was not kept) and decomposed over J++ instead of the J-lens, so part B's J-space matches the second reader part A uses. Chosen by the human.

topup.rule: the one allowed top-up round: new prompts only for these entities, nothing removed, same checks on the merged set; the whole pipeline is re-run because the grand mean depends on which entities have probes
